themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 46 THIS WEEK versus an 8-week average of 8.0 per week—a 475% increase (z-score: 7.84)—indicating a sudden deterioration in road quality across Crown Heights/Prospect Heights that demands immediate investigation into what triggered the spike.
evidence: 46 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Accompanied by spike in dangling street sign complaints (7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 avg, z-score: 6.43)
reporting_angles: What caused this sudden deterioration—weather, deferred maintenance, construction, or budget cuts?
Are specific neighborhoods or block clusters more affected than others?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints jumped to 14 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 4.6 per week—a 203% spike (z-score: 4.85)—signaling either a new dumping operation or enforcement gap in sanitation oversight that residents are rapidly reporting.
evidence: 14 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with community board's repeated budget requests for 'other cleaning requests' to Department of Sanitation, suggesting chronic understaffing
reporting_angles: Where are the hotspots—are they near construction sites, vacant lots, or specific commercial corridors?
Is DSNY responding to complaints, and what is their response timeline?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk & Street Noise Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Street/sidewalk noise complaints climbed to 26 LAST WEEK from a 10.5-per-week average—a 148% spike (z-score: 3.94)—while residential noise remains elevated at 1,112 complaints over 90 days, suggesting ongoing quality-of-life deterioration linked to street-level activity.
evidence: 26 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 10.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (148% spike, z-score: 3.94)
Residential noise is the 3rd-highest complaint category overall (1,112 complaints in 90 days)
Real-time enforcement complaints also spiked to 7 THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 avg (331% increase), suggesting police/enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: What types of street activity are driving complaints—construction, commercial loading, street vendors, or nightlife venues?
Are NYPD or local enforcement agencies responding to the spike in enforcement complaints?

themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Signs & Safety Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street sign complaints exploded to 7 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 0.6 per week—a 1020% spike (z-score: 6.43)—representing a sudden municipal infrastructure safety hazard that could affect pedestrian and vehicle safety.
evidence: 7 dangling street sign complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Follows street condition spike, suggesting broader infrastructure deterioration event or weather damage
reporting_angles: Did a recent weather event (high winds, snow load) cause the damage?
How quickly is DOT responding to repair requests, and are residents experiencing related safety incidents?

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 11 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 3.0 per week—a 267% increase (z-score: 4.44)—suggesting potential HVAC failures, mold, or environmental contamination in residential or commercial buildings that warrants health investigation.
evidence: 11 indoor air quality complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 3.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Heat/hot water complaints remain the highest category (3,760 in 90 days), suggesting heating system issues may be driving secondary air quality problems
reporting_angles: Are specific buildings or addresses showing patterns, or is this district-wide?
Are complaints tied to heating system malfunctions, mold growth, or outdoor air pollution sources?
